Speed is a scalar quantity that refers to how fast an object is moving, regardless of its direction or orientation. It's simply the distance traveled per unit time without considering any specific direction in which it moves. Velocity, on the other hand, is a vector quantity and takes into account both magnitude (speed) as well as the direction of motion.
